People are tribal and individualism only goes so far. There is a human need to belong to a tribe of some sort. For so much of human existence, a lot of this identity formation involved occupations, to the point where such things as [occupational surnames](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Category:Occupational_surnames) evolved in the language. You literally were called by name with reference to what you did -- Fisher, Carpenter, Baker, Bishop, Smith, etc.

But surnames notwithstanding, now that jobs are scarce, and growing scarcer due to automation (to the point where even illegals, H1Bs, and Chinese toddlers will get replaced by HAL 9000), and there's one side of the aisle that wants to [do away with the very idea of work](https://www.marxists.org/archive/lafargue/1883/lazy/) altogether because it's inherently "unequal" and "oppressive" and *can't* be reformed except through the "capitalist system," people start forming their identities around some personal characteristic rather than profession -- because they don't have a job to begin with, and they don't want to admit that they *are* nothing because they *do* nothing.

This may be one reason why the whole idea of whites as a racial voting bloc never took off: Whites are too busy working, keeping busy, earning a living, to identify themselves by their race, whereas minorities don't have high rates of employment, and far too many of them come from a culture of entitlement that says they shouldn't have to work at all because "we" took everything of "theirs" and now we should have to "give it back." Blacks see us as "whitey," Hispanics as "gringo," Muslims as "infidel," Jews as "goyim" -- and this baffles us because we're a largely individualistic culture, especially in the U.S., and we just see ourselves as "Bob, the builder" or "Joe, the plumber" or "Jane, his wife."

Now, there are some minority individuals who see themselves as individuals, and define themselves by their accomplishments or occupations rather than personal characteristics, but even they are often branded traitors -- minorities within a minority -- by the "culture" that sees them as having defined themselves as something other than their *kin*, but not as an individual, as a member of the "enemy" tribe that doesn't even see itself as a "tribe" in the first place and is thus bizarre.

But now that whites are losing that definition they/we had for so long because there are no jobs to "label" ourselves by, we're finally seeing the rise of a dispossessed white voting bloc gathering around Trump, who wants to restore their "identities" as workers with good wages, and put "Americans first." He doesn't even really mention whites. He just mentions work. But this angers the ethnic voting blocs who don't see themselves as "Americans" first at all, but as whatever their primary "tribe" is ahead of their country of residence and the job they (don't) work while living there: the hyphenated-American who identifies with Africa, Mexico or even Islam rather than simply America and its values of hard work and individualism.

Why? Because according to them, these are values that whites identify with. Blacks go with "the hood," Latins with "familia," Muslims with "the ummah," and Jews with "the chosen people." White Americans and White Europeans are just Bob the builder, not Bob the Polish-German-Czechoslovakian-American. Bob says, why should I identify with Poland? I don't live or work in Poland. The closest I've ever been to Poland is to drink some Poland Spring during a break on the *job*.

But now there are some, usually white *liberals*, who feel left out of the whole minority tribes trend, but they either don't have a job, or don't *want* a job, or don't want to identify themselves by their job *if* they have one. In that case, they come up with something else to coalesce around: who they fuck and/or what appendages are in their pants. If Bob wants to join the collectivism crowd, he becomes Bob the *gay* builder first and foremost in his mind, or Roberta, the builder formerly known as Bob. He starts demanding special gifts and allowances be made for him not because he is a good builder, but because he has a "condition," or an "orientation," or some other squishy trait that doesn't have any bearing on his ability to do his job -- but, he says (zee says?), does impact his ability to "negotiate space." Whatever that means.

So what I see as being a solution to identity politics is to find a way for people to work more jobs -- but have some kind of contractual obligation restricting identitarianism on the grounds that it's bad for morale. Shut up about your sex life, your bathroom preference, and/or whatever happened on the Amistad or during the Crusades or oy vey the Shoah. This is the elephant in the room that Congress, for whatever reason, just won't take up. A final solution to the bathroom problem: take a shit behind closed doors and don't make it a political issue. Get back in the closet except among close friends. Take off your head scarf and hide your crucifix jewelry under your clothes. Skin color isn't as easy to hide, but it's very easy not to make a big issue of either. Nothing is holding you back but your attitude and your unwillingness to put America first, or your job first, or your efforts into finding a job -- not because you "deserve" one due to who you *are*, but because you'd be good at it because that's what you *do*.

To Make America Great Again, we need to make Americans Americans again. That means Bob the builder is just Bob the builder. He does belong to a tribe, but that tribe is Local 1234 Builders' Association. Not Local 1234 1/2 Gay Transgender Builders' Association of the Former Yugoslavia and the YMCA.
